name: Rhizome
summary: Rhizome is PlantPal's atlas-class design system. The garden is a world on one plane: every plant, species, problem, treatment course and journal entry is a node on a fixed lattice, joined by veins that are drawn before they are travelled. Navigation is a rescale of that plane, never a route. This file is the register: the laws, the numbers and the page scope. Any page in this system that cites a C-number is citing THIS file.

sources_of_record.invariants: constitution.json -> invariants[]. A page quotes the statement verbatim and adds its own verification; it never paraphrases it into a second wording.
sources_of_record.parameters: constitution.json -> parameters. Mirrored into assets/tokens.css as --rz-param-* and into assets/system.js as RZ.PARAMS. RZ.verifyParameters() reads the computed CSS values back and reports disagreement, so the copies cannot silently drift.

invariants.statement: Every navigation follows an edge that was visible before the click.
invariants.how_to_check: Iterate every control that calls RZ.go(target); assert every consecutive pair of RZ.route(focus, target) is present in the edge list and has a drawn .rz-vein in the DOM at first paint.

invariants.statement: After any hop, the origin is still on screen or exactly one visible hop back -- with no reliance on a history stack or browser back.
invariants.how_to_check: After any RZ.go, assert the previous focus still has a rendered element carrying a rank attribute, and that it appears in the Navigate-to list of the new focus or is joined to it by one drawn vein. Assert history.length is unchanged.

invariants.statement: On a focus change the surrounding nodes change to that node's own neighbours, every drawn edge is actually traversable, and the neighbour count tracks real degree.
invariants.how_to_check: For every node assert RZ.adj[id].length equals the number of drawn veins touching it and equals the number printed in the Navigate-to header.

invariants.statement: Nothing is replaced, unmounted, or routed to -- every navigation is a rescale.
invariants.how_to_check: Record the node element set before and after ten hops; the sets are the identical objects. Nothing is added to or removed from the plane, and location.href never changes.

invariants.statement: Where the user is, is answerable at every zoom level without hovering or reading -- by a position marker in the persistent world view, not by a breadcrumb alone.
invariants.how_to_check: At zoom.min and zoom.max assert the world view's you-are-here marker is inside the world-view frame and its coordinates equal the mapped position of the focused node.

invariants.statement: This surface is still the right regime under Sec.4's discriminator -- dense, meaningful, user-traversed cross-relationships, a real graph and not a hierarchy wearing one.
invariants.how_to_check: Assert the edge list contains cross-branch edges (a journal entry to the plant it is about; two problems sharing one treatment course) so the graph is not a tree, and that edge count >= node count.

invariants.statement: Two consecutive loads of the same graph lay out identically, with positions derived deterministically and persisted -- never from a live simulation or render order.
invariants.how_to_check: Load twice and diff the computed left/top of every node element; they are equal. Reverse the DOM order of the node elements and reload: positions are unchanged.

invariants.statement: Inserting a node leaves existing nodes put, and the design states its placement rule, its density strategy, and its growth ceiling.
invariants.how_to_check: Append a node at a free cell and reload; every pre-existing node's computed left/top is unchanged. layout-determinism.json states all three rules.

invariants.statement: No non-structural data change (status, count, new attachment) moves anything.
invariants.how_to_check: Mutate a node's status, recap and count; diff every node's computed left/top before and after. Nothing moves, and the world-view extent is unchanged.

invariants.statement: Every focus change travels -- nothing fades, pops, or teleports.
invariants.how_to_check: Sample the camera transform each frame during a hop: more than two distinct positions are sampled and the first equals the pre-hop camera.

invariants.statement: Every transition carries direction, scale, and ownership -- and the camera follows the edge's own path.
invariants.how_to_check: Sample the camera centre each frame and assert every sample lies on the polyline of the route's real edges within one pixel.

invariants.statement: With the text blurred on a frozen frame, the hierarchy is still readable from scale alone, on the 100/75/55/30/18-25 ladder.
invariants.how_to_check: Apply a 6px blur to the plane and screenshot: the four rank widths remain four distinguishable sizes and the kind graduation on each card head is still separable by length.

invariants.statement: Under prefers-reduced-motion, direction is still shown and the you-are-here still updated -- with no transition replaced by an abrupt swap.
invariants.how_to_check: Set data-motion="reduced" and hop: the trail along the real edges is drawn and held, and both the world-view marker and its accessible label have moved.

invariants.statement: A user can tell navigation from mutation before activating it, from form alone.
invariants.how_to_check: Screenshot every affordance with its text masked: each is either a filled stake (mutation) or an outlined chip with a caret (traversal), and no third form exists outside the camera cluster.

invariants.statement: No mutating affordance moves the camera, no navigation affordance changes data, and no dialog contains a traversal.
invariants.how_to_check: Activate every stake and assert the camera transform is identical afterwards. Activate every chip and assert no record field changed. Assert no element inside a dialog calls RZ.go.

invariants.statement: There is exactly one focal point, it owns the camera, and the camera never moves without a user-attributable reason.
invariants.how_to_check: Assert exactly one element carries data-focus="true". Idle the page 60s and assert the camera transform is unchanged.

invariants.statement: Nothing other than the focused node's body scrolls.
invariants.how_to_check: For every element in the document assert scrollHeight > clientHeight holds only for the focused node's body, and that document.body has no scrollbar.

invariants.statement: Every edge can be traversed by keyboard, following the graph rather than DOM order -- and a screen reader can announce the focus and its connections.
invariants.how_to_check: For each neighbour of the focus assert some arrow direction proposes it and that the choice is computed from neighbour positions, not document order. Assert the live-region text after a hop names origin, crossings and new degree.

invariants.statement: The focused node answers all four questions without further navigation.
invariants.how_to_check: On the focused card locate a block answering each of: what is this, what state is it in, what can I do here, where can I go from here -- all present in the card and its two adjacent chrome panels without a hop.

invariants.statement: Leaving to settings runs the exit choreography -- camera out, app shrinks to a floating card, panel beside it -- rather than a centred modal over a blur.
invariants.how_to_check: Open settings and assert the shell carries transform scale(0.42) translateX(-25%), the settings panel is a sibling on the same plane at the same depth, and no role=dialog or backdrop-filter overlay exists.

invariants.statement: Search and notification arrivals show the distance being crossed rather than cutting to the destination.
invariants.how_to_check: Trigger a search arrival and a notification arrival: both announce the hop count first and both drive the same RZ.travel path as a card click. Instrument RZ.travel to prove one code path.

invariants.statement: At >=10s the geography holds, with per-node loading in place and no repositioning as nodes resolve.
invariants.how_to_check: Set data-speed="slow" and diff every node's computed left/top before and after: nothing moves, no global overlay exists, and each unresolved node carries its own skeleton at the real row heights.

invariants.statement: On a partial graph, unloaded regions are drawn as explicitly unknown -- distinguishable from "loaded and empty" -- with traversal into them allowed and never dead-ending.
invariants.how_to_check: Assert an unknown node and an empty node are both present and materially different, that the unknown node offers a real fetch control, and that RZ.go into it succeeds.

invariants.statement: Offline, the last-known world is navigable, staleness is honest per node, mutations are explicitly refused or queued, and geography stays put.
invariants.how_to_check: Set data-net="offline": every hop still works, at least two nodes state DIFFERENT staleness in their own words, every stake is visibly refused or announces itself queued, and no node moved.

invariants.statement: On failure the error is a state inside the node, with retry in place and the camera undisturbed.
invariants.how_to_check: Put a node into the error state: the fact, the time, the fate of the user's data, a retry and a second way through are all inside that node's body, and the camera transform is unchanged.

invariants.statement: Day zero reads as a world with room in it, with the first node landing in a place it will keep.
invariants.how_to_check: Render the empty garden: the lattice shows free cells around the single node, and that node's cell equals the cell it still holds after twelve plants are added.

laws.name: Chrome is a register, not a layer
Mutation and traversal are tellable apart before you click
Rank is computed, and scale carries it
The node is a contract, not a card
The edge list is the single source of truth
The board pans, the node reads
The background belongs to the surface it decorates
Leaving the app is a choreography, not a modal
Degradation is material on the board, and the geography never degrades
A reviewer must be able to walk the states

amendments.policy: A theme round MAY add a token family or a primitive under a named amendment and MUST record it in register[] below. It may not remove or re-key an existing semantic token, and it may not change a parameter above without an owner ruling. A page-writing agent modifies nothing else under assets/.

entry_shape.reason: <why the existing vocabulary could not carry it>

register.reason: Chrome is position: fixed by contract (L1: it sits flush to a VIEWPORT edge and never moves with the camera). A documentation stage is not a viewport, so an assembled specimen — the world with its whole chrome register around it — had no way to hold its own chrome. The existing vocabulary could not carry it: no class in system.css or docs.css established a containing block, and the alternatives were worse (putting chrome inside .rz-plane would make it move with the camera, and data-mode="overview" would run the settings-exit choreography on a docs page). The transform establishes a containing block for fixed descendants and moves nothing.
